title: St. Bartholomew's Cathedral in Frankfurt, Germany
caption: Ghosts of empires past
subtitle: It's Halloween!
description: Frankfurt, Germany, provides a fitting backdrop for Halloween with St. Bartholomew's Cathedral and its striking Gothic tower. Yet the holiday's origins are even more intriguing. Many Halloween traditions are linked to Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival marking the end of the harvest season and the start of winter. People believed the boundary between the living and the dead grew thin, prompting bonfires, offerings and disguises to ward off wandering spirits. Later, the Christian observances of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day helped shape Halloween as we know it today. St. Bartholomew's may set the scene, but Halloween brings the ghosts, legends and mystery.

title: Black Forest, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
caption: Mist among the trees
subtitle: Black Forest, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
description: The Black Forest in south-west Germany is known for its misty landscapes, forested hills, deep valleys, lakes and picturesque towns. Stretching about 160 kilometres, the region is home to Feldberg, its highest peak at 1,493 metres, and marks the source of both the Danube and Neckar rivers. Beyond its natural beauty, the Black Forest is rich in history and tradition. Forestry has shaped the region for centuries, while its renowned clockmaking heritage helped make the cuckoo clock famous around the world. Today, the area remains one of Germany's most distinctive destinations, blending cultural heritage with striking scenery.

title: Polar bear and cubs by Hudson Bay, Manitoba, Canada
caption: A future written in ice
subtitle: Polar Bear Week
description: November marks an important time for polar bears along the shores of Hudson Bay in Manitoba, where they gather and wait for sea ice to form before returning to hunt seals. This annual event is celebrated during Polar Bear Week, observed in early November. Polar bears are powerful swimmers and highly adapted to Arctic life, but shrinking sea ice is forcing many to spend more time on land, making it harder to find food. The mother and cubs seen in today's image represent generations of bears that have followed this seasonal cycle, highlighting both the beauty of the Arctic and the importance of protecting the habitat these iconic Canadian animals depend on.

title: Lake Braies, Fanes‑Sennes‑Braies Nature Park, Dolomites, Italy
caption: Peace among the peaks
subtitle: Lake Braies, Dolomites, Italy
description: Lake Braies sits almost 1,500 metres above sea level in the Dolomites of South Tyrol, northern Italy. Surrounded by forest and the dramatic peaks of the Fanes-Sennes-Braies Nature Park, the lake is known for its striking green and blue waters. A 3.5-kilometre trail circles the shore, while traditional wooden rowing boats offer another way to take in the scenery. The lake is also a starting point for several mountain walks, including the Dolomites' famous Alta Via 1.

title: People rowing among colourful bald cypress, Xuancheng, Anhui, China
caption: Paddling a painted forest
subtitle: Colourful bald cypress, Xuancheng, Anhui, China
description: People paddle through flooded woodlands in Xuancheng, Anhui, where fall transforms bald cypress forests into a striking display of amber, copper and rust-coloured foliage. Unlike most conifers, bald cypress sheds its soft needles each fall after they turn reddish-brown. Native to North America, these trees thrive in wetlands, swamps and floodplains, often developing distinctive root "knees" that rise above the water. Some specimens have lived for more than 1,000 years. In late fall, the still water reflects the colourful canopy above, creating a remarkable landscape that highlights the bald cypress's natural connection to wetland environments.

title: Wooden stile at a stone wall, Black Crag, Lake District, England
caption: One step closer to the summit
subtitle: Black Crag, Lake District, England
description: A simple wooden gate opens onto the Lake District, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in north-west England known for its lakes, rolling hills and centuries-old stone walls. This path leads toward Black Crag, the summit of Black Fell, which rises to about 323 metres and offers impressive views of Windermere, Coniston Water, and the Langdale Pikes. The route passes Tarn Hows, one of the region's most scenic spots, before climbing through a landscape shaped by nature and farming traditions. Some trails also follow Tom Gill, where woodland paths run alongside cascading waterfalls in this picturesque corner of Cumbria.

title: Bamboo forest, Pīpīwai Trail, Haleakalā National Park, Maui, Hawaii, USA
caption: A green tunnel through Maui
subtitle: Bamboo forest, Haleakalā National Park, Maui, Hawaii
description: Haleakalā National Park on Maui is home to an extraordinary mix of landscapes, from volcanic slopes and rainforest to towering bamboo forests. The park stretches from the summit of Haleakalā, which rises 3,055 metres above sea level, to the Pacific coast. More than 850 plant species grow here, including some found nowhere else on Earth, alongside native Hawaiian wildlife. One of the park's most popular walks is the Pīpīwai Trail, which winds through lush forest before reaching a remarkable bamboo grove. As the bamboo sways in the breeze, its tall stalks create distinctive sounds that add to the unique experience.

title: A bison in the grasslands of Theodore Roosevelt National Park, North Dakota, USA
caption: The giant that came back
description: One of North America's most remarkable animals, the bison is a powerful symbol of strength, resilience and conservation. Weighing as much as 900 kilograms (2,000 pounds) and capable of running up to 55 km/h (35 mph), bison are surprisingly agile. Despite being commonly called buffalo, American bison are a distinct species known for their massive shoulder hump, curved horns and shaggy coats that help them thrive through harsh winters. Once pushed to the brink of extinction, bison have made an inspiring comeback thanks to conservation efforts across Canada and the United States, making them a powerful example of successful wildlife recovery.
